newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels warn of more killings.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels warn of more killings.

text.p: The leader of Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA) has warned that his Islamic rebel group will step up attacks in Algeria during the holy fasting month of Ramadan, an Algerian newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"The war will continue and will be intensified during the month of Ramadan. We have the means and the men to punish all those who are not on our side," GIA leader Antar Zouabri said in a statement posted on the walls of some mosques in northern Algeria and quoted by El Watan newspaper.

At least 150 people have been killed and more than 170 wounded in Algeria since the start of Ramadan on January 10. Militant fundamentalists regard the Moslem month of fasting as the month of "jihad" -- holy war -- against the secular military-backed government.

A car bomb ripped through a working-class area in Algiers on Sunday evening. The newspaper Liberte on Tuesday put the death toll at 42 with more than 100 wounded. The authorities had said 21 people were killed. One leading newspaper dubbed the bombing a "Ramadan massacre".

Analysts believe the killings are a message to President Liamine Zeroual, as well as to Algerians, that the fundamentalists are still a formidable force despite repeated claims by the government that it has crushed the guerrillas.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
